messages:
skyler: FYI noticed a weird pattern in us-west2-rack8 last night: multiple dedicated-slice allocations got transiently routed through the same set of nodes and p99 for small-gen requests spiked to >400ms for ~8m. Not classic noisy-host.
jo: link to grafana panels? which metrics spiked?
skyler: infra.net_tx_drop, infra.nic_tx_qlen, allocator.routing_multipath_conflicts. timeline: 2025-03-16T22:05 -> 22:13 UTC. Also saw a surge of `alloc_attempts` for dsp-usw2-b.
infra-bot: scheduler-bot: high_res_timer_mode=on at 2025-03-16T22:04:59Z (rolling kernel tuning commit KERN-587)
viktor: oh nice catch. We flipped the scheduler HRT patch on that AZ to reduce latency for small-batch training. Could HRT cause more synchronized wakeups and thus coalesce tx bursts on the NIC?
skyler: that's the hypothesis. NIC tx queue length went from 32 -> 1024 transiently; egress pacing couldn't keep up, causing queuing on the switch and backpressure into proxies.
leah: do we have any perf logs from the switch? was ECN marking happening?
jo: switch counters show tail drops on the leaf for that rack and increased tail latency. ECN ramped briefly.
viktor: mitigation suggestions:
- revert high_res_timer_mode on the rack (short term)
- apply `ethtool -C eth0 rx-usecs` tuning to smooth irq coalescing on affected hosts
- add allocator anti-sync: jitter hotfill timing per-AZ to avoid simultaneous handoffs
- probe to prefer nodes with `nic_tx_headroom` label when assigning handoff traffic
skyler: I ran a quick canary: toggled HRT off on rack8 at 22:12 and latency dropped to normal over 90s. That suggests timer alignment was the trigger.
infra-bot: billing-bot: egress-anomaly detected: dsp-usw2-b egress bytes increased 1.7x in window 22:05-22:13. Estimated incremental cost $340 for that spike.
leah: short-term rollback + ops note to finance. For dedicated customers affected (tenant IDs attached) we should consider internal credit or cost-share if our rollback plan caused re-routes.
viktor: longer-term: allocator needs anti-synchronous logic. Ideas:
- add jitter on hotfill schedule: sample from exp dist (mean 200ms) before bulk moves
- consult node-level `timer_mode` and avoid moving latency-sensitive flows to nodes with HRT enabled if they are known to sync
- expose `egress_penalty` in node metadata to bias routing away from recently-bursty nodes
jo: also consider a switch-side mitigation: enable pacing or policer per-port to avoid huge microbursts eating buffer and causing cross-tenant harm. But that might increase latency for bursty jobs.
skyler: created INFRA-1290 with notes, logs, grafana links, owners: viktor (allocator changes), leah (billing touchpoint), jo (switch config follow-up), skyler (canary rollback doc). Added timeline and diff of kernel tunables.
viktor: i'll prototype jitter hotfill + node telemetry lookup. Can we get a dataset of historical hotfills vs timer_mode? need to understand freq.
leah: finance will review cost impact and ping tenants. also flag dedicated-sla impacts to support.
jo: re: switch pacing, i'll open a ticket with networking to test per-port pacing in lab and simulate synchronized bursts.
infra-bot: followup-reminder set for 24h.
skyler: TL;DR: enabling high-res timer in rack synchronized wakeups -> NIC tx bursts -> switch tail drops -> proxy/backpressure and egress cost spike. Rollback helped; work items created to add allocator anti-sync, node metadata signals, and switch pacing experiments. :spiral_notepad:
